business_problem: Schwarz Group needed a cloud database service for STACKIT that could support Lidl's automatic goods ordering workload, keep customer data under EU jurisdiction, and absorb more than 100 GB of data per day from 500 sources without rigid schemas.
solution_summary: Schwarz Group built STACKIT, a cloud platform hosted in its own German and Austrian data centers, and selected MongoDB Enterprise Advanced as the document database layer for both internal and external customers. The design had to ingest more than 100 GB of data per day from 500 sources, absorb read/write peaks, and support Lidl's auto-dispo ordering workflow without exposing customer data to foreign jurisdictions. MongoDB's document model lets STACKIT MongoDB store nested retail and supply-chain data without rigid schemas, while containerized deployments and historized schema rollbacks simplify rollout and rollback on the platform. By packaging MongoDB as a managed STACKIT service, Schwarz IT can serve Group workloads and external customers with EU data residency, transparent cost controls, and a scalable alternative to hyperscalers.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Provides the document database foundation for STACKIT to store and scale complex retail and supply-chain data.

solution_components.name: STACKIT MongoDB
solution_components.role: Exposes MongoDB as a managed service on STACKIT so internal teams and external customers can deploy NoSQL workloads quickly.

data_flow: Retail and supply-chain data from hundreds of sources flows into STACKIT MongoDB, where document storage and indexing support Lidl's auto-dispo ordering workflows and other customer applications. The managed service then serves internal Schwarz Group teams and external customers from EU-hosted cloud infrastructure.
business_outcome: MongoDB lets STACKIT support large-scale auto-dispo workloads, open a new cloud-services revenue stream, guarantee EU data residency, and give Lidl teams transparent minute-level visibility into cost and performance.
